attempted_claim: Let P^n(2)=S^{n-1} union_2 e^n (n>=3) and n=4m+1 with m>=2. Decide the finite exact bound: is 4·π_k(P^n(2))=0 for all k ≤ 4n−7, equivalently is the 4th power map 4: Ω^2 P^n(2) → Ω^2 P^n(2) null-homotopic after restriction to sk_{4n−9}(Ω^2 P^n(2))? In Goodwillie–EHP terms: does the Goodwillie-filtration/P-map and Hopf-invariant obstruction analysis force this null-homotopy, or does a detected EHP class carry a Z/8-summand in this range?
decisive_failure: The 4-vs-8 decision needs the unstable 2-primary EHP P-map differentials, James-Hopf correction terms, and Toda data for S^{4m} in degrees up to 4n-7, which local deduction cannot supply; the attempted Whitehead/Hilton detectors provably vanish by finiteness and Jacobi torsion. No literature search was used and no emergent claim is asserted.
